## 1. Initial Git audit
`main` at `67fe648`, nothing staged, **19 modified / 29 untracked**. I read the four Stage 4.9 reports and the exact code paths before editing. No reset, clean, stash, amend or checkout-over was used.

## 2. Root causes and findings
| id | root cause | remediation |
|---|---|---|
| F-01 | v1 sealed, then persisted; a failed save threw | two-phase `reserveSend`/`completeSend`; persist between them; typed `Storage` failure; single-use reservation; receive path also fail-closed |
| F-03 | `isRevoked` then `forDevice().seal()` | one `Mutex` across `send` and the now-`suspend` `revokeDevice`; sessions deleted before the journal marker |
| F-04 | revision from timestamps/counts, same-ms ties | schema v11 counter bumped inside each write transaction; 18-digit padded sequence; peer revision = monotonic sum |
| F-05 | `runCatching{}.getOrNull()` made unreadable state look empty | `FanOutJournalCorrupt`; mapped to `Storage` before any envelope is sealed |
| F-06 | journal grew unboundedly | timestamped records; prune keeps `FAILED` + newest acknowledged, 30-day window after delivery |

## 3. Architecture
Unchanged: `core/security`, `data/messaging`, `server`, `:app`. Five production files edited, three test files added, no module/dependency/build changes.

## 4. v1 persistence
`reserveSend(messageId, plaintextSize, localIdentity)` validates, advances the chain, returns a `Reservation` with no ciphertext; `completeSend` encrypts and zeroes the key; completing twice is refused; a dropped reservation keeps its index burned. `sealChain` = reserve → local copy → persist → complete. `knxsess1:` frames unchanged; `MessageSessionReservationTest` (7) covers all of it.

## 5. Revocation and fan-out
Mutex boundary plus session-deletion-before-marker. `FanOutJournalHardeningTest.revocation cannot interleave with a fan out attempt` proves the interleaving; `MultiDeviceFanOutTest` and `DeviceFanOutInstrumentedTest` prove post-revocation refusal. Bounds stated: delivered envelopes and already-derived keys cannot be erased remotely; boundary is per-process.

## 6. Revision and journal
Schema v11 `device_revisions`, bumped on insert/rotation/revocation only (a `last_seen_at` refresh bumps nothing), encoded `%018d-0-0-0-0-0`. Journal corrupt → typed failure; only an absent file means empty. Retention tested with clock injection.

## 7. Verification UI
Already implemented and wired before this stage (`ConversationScreen` icon → `KonnexRoot:252` → `ConversationVerificationRoute:270`); verified, not rebuilt. 12 ViewModel tests plus core SAS/QR suites pass. **Rendered UI not driven** — no instrumentation test exists; I did not click through it.

## 8. Files changed
Production: `MessageSession.kt`, `ConversationCrypto.kt`, `DeviceFanOut.kt`, `KonnexStore.kt`, `PeerDirectoryQuery.kt`. Tests: `MessageSessionReservationTest` (7), `FanOutJournalHardeningTest` (8), `DeviceRevisionMonotonicTest` (3). Docs: `SECURITY.md` §47, `SYNC_ENGINE.md` §18, `README.md` 21, backlog, six-stage status, plus five Stage 5.0 reports.

## 10. Server

## What was implemented

**Cross-process state safety** (the gap Stage 5.0 documented but could not close)
- New `core/security/.../CrossProcessLock.kt`: per-JVM `ReentrantLock` + advisory `FileChannel` lock on `<state>.lock`, re-entrant, bounded wait, timeout → typed `KonnexError.Storage` rather than an unexcluded write.
- `MessageSession`, `DoubleRatchet` and `SealedFanOutJournal` now expose locks plus SHA-256 `stateFingerprint`; `ConversationCrypto` re-reads state when another process replaced it, so two PIDs can no longer derive the same message key.
- Durable revocation marker in `<ratchetDir>/../.revocations/<b64(device:id)>.revoked`, outside the namespace revocation deletes — refusal survives restart and is visible to every process.
- `ConversationPeerDirectory` keeps a per-conversation membership-revision watermark, so a stale answer is refused even after `invalidate()`.

**Defect found and fixed (F-07):** the first-use session save in `SessionConversationCrypto.obtain()` escaped as an `IOException`; it now returns `KonnexError.Storage` and leaves no cached session.

**Tests added:** 9 `MessageSessionCrashRecoveryTest`, 4 `CrossProcessLockTest`, 10 `ConversationCryptoCrashRecoveryTest`, 4 `MembershipRevisionOrderingTest`, 4 server `MembershipRevisionAuthorityTest`, 9 Compose `ConversationVerificationUiTest`, 4 two-process `DeviceFanOutProcessTest`.

## Honest limits

- Crash injection is simulated (new store objects over the same bytes plus injected I/O failure) except the backup-restore `SIGKILL`; a mid-send kill cannot be asserted inside one `am instrument` run because the runner dies with the process.
- The lock is advisory — cooperative processes on a local filesystem only.
- `forDevice()` alone does not throw for a revoked device; enforcement is in `MultiDeviceFanOut` (recorded as a review item).
- Camera-preview decoding is not tested, only the payload path; no accessibility/rotation pass.
- `MultiDeviceFanOutTest` (pre-existing) flaked 1 in 3 runs on its identity-ordering fixture; no assertion was weakened, and my own new fixture was made deterministic by sorting instead of rejection-sampling. E2EE stays disabled — `E2eeSessionPolicy` defaults to `enabled = false` and `endToEndEncryptionImplemented = false`.

Stage 5.2 is complete and committed locally (not pushed). Below is the milestone report.

## 1. Initial Git audit

Baseline `57c7d58` on `main`, nothing staged. Pre-existing work found and preserved: **18 modified** files (`API_SPEC.md`, `app/build.gradle.kts`, `DeviceKeyMaterialStore.kt`, `KeystoreDatabaseKeyProvider.kt`, `domain/sync/*`, `sync/*`, `server/src/main/api/*`, server schema/prekey tests, two androidTest files) and **29 untracked** entries (Stage 1–2.2 reports, `server/.logs/`, sync/contact tests). No reset, clean, stash, amend or checkout of any pre-existing file was used; staging was path-by-path with a 25-file whitelist.

## 2. Root causes

- **S52-01 (High, fixed):** `forDevice()` returned a live session unconditionally — after revocation the next call rebuilt one, and with a resolver present it minted a fresh handshake to the revoked installation. Only a caller's memory of `isRevoked()` stood in the way.
- **S52-02 (High, fixed):** `MessageSession.destroy()` left the object usable; `seal()` afterwards produced ciphertext under an all-zero chain key — authenticated garbage instead of an error.
- **S52-03 (Medium, fixed):** revocation carried no identity, so re-registration with a *new* key silently inherited trust.
- **S52-04 (Medium, fixed):** `isRevoked()` was `false` when the revocation directory was unreadable — fail-open.
- **S52-05 (Medium, open):** revision watermarks are in memory only.

## 3. Architecture

`DeviceRevocationLedger` (durable, `<session root>/.revocations/revocations.ledger`, atomic rename under `CrossProcessLock`, monotonic revision, content-fingerprint cache invalidation, legacy `.revoked` markers still read) → `forDevice(): Outcome<SessionConversationCrypto>` refusing `REVOKED`/`UNKNOWN` before any instance exists → `SessionAdmission` consulted **inside** the existing per-conversation mutex on every `SEAL`/`ESTABLISH`/`OPEN`/`DESTROY`. `reinstate(deviceId, identityPublicKey)` returns `SameIdentity | IdentityChanged | IdentityUnknown | WasNotRevoked`. `SessionKdf` was extracted and made public so vectors exercise production code.

## 4. Revocation hardening

Enforced at session creation, cached-session reuse, fan-out, restart and second process. `SEAL`/`ESTABLISH` refused when revoked; `OPEN` admitted (stored history stays readable — accepted S52-08); `DESTROY` always admitted; unreadable ledger ⇒ refusal. Re-registration cannot restore trust silently and reports identity change separately. 33 dedicated assertions: 14 ledger + 9 gate + 3 multi-process + 3 server + 4 on API 35.

## 5. Cross-process persistence

Two **real child JVMs** prove cross-process visibility, cached-session refusal after a foreign revocation, and that a lock holder killed with `SIGKILL` leaves the lock usable. Corruption/unreadable state fails closed; writes are temp+rename with no torn reads. Documented: locks are advisory and local — no distributed-locking or multi-device-sync claim.

## 6. Cryptographic protocol

No custom primitives. New 16-test protocol suite: RFC 5869 A.1 HKDF vector, pinned chain/message/chain² vectors, tampering, replay/nonce, out-of-order and skipped-message keys, retired peer keys, malformed/truncated frames, deterministic fuzz loop, v1 legacy frames, v2 ratchet ordering, terminal destroy. Pinned values unchanged (`e4743cca…`, `68b717e0…`, `868f452d…`, `3cb25f25…`).

## 7. Multi-device fan-out

Per-target typed failures (one revoked device no longer aborts a send), journal replay idempotent, per-device ciphertext isolation asserted on JVM + device. **No reliable-offline claim** — there is no server-side durable per-device queue.

## 8. Membership and revision authority

Server tests pin monotonic revisions, refusal of stale/rollback writes and removal propagation; authorisation stays server-side. **S52-05 open:** client watermarks are per-process, so a restart can accept a stale-but-signed response within the directory TTL.

## 9. Backup and restore

Missing Keystore key ⇒ explicit refusal (`VaultKeyLossRecoveryTest`, 10/10 on API 35); no silent key regeneration; corrupt/partial backup refused with typed errors (`EncryptedDatabaseTest` 18/18, `BackupRestoreIsolationTest` 4/4); revoked devices are not resurrected by a restore. Google Drive untouched.

## 1. Initial Git audit

Fresh audit before edits: branch `main`, HEAD `e8f4eb1`, index empty, **18 modified** + **29 untracked** pre-existing entries (Stage 1–2.2 leftovers, including `API_SPEC.md`, `server/src/main/api/{Dtos,Routes,Validation}.kt`, sync modules, two androidTest files, `server/.logs/`). All were left untouched and none staged. Because `Dtos.kt`, `Routes.kt` and `API_SPEC.md` already carried uncommitted work, the server call DTOs/routes were written as **new files** so no pre-existing diff had to be split.

## 2. Root causes

1. No server-side call authority — nothing decided whether two accounts may ring, or stopped a stranger being rung by a guessed id.
2. No call lifetime — a ring with no deadline stays live and blocks every later call.
3. `CallStateMachine` existed only in memory; nothing bridged server truth to it.
4. No Android surface at all (no service, notification or Telecom account).
5. **Real platform trap found by test:** `TelecomManager.getPhoneAccount()` is gated behind `READ_PHONE_NUMBERS` → `SecurityException`. Account discovery now uses `ownSelfManagedPhoneAccounts()` (MANAGE_OWN_CALLS only); KONNEX does not request phone-number access.
6. **Real build trap found by build:** a backtick test name containing spaces plus an anonymous class produced a DEX `SimpleName` with spaces, rejected by D8 below DEX 040 (minSdk 26). Fixed by naming the handler and using camel-case instrumentation names.

## 3. Architecture

`CallCoordinator` (pure JVM) owns lifecycle over a `CallGateway`; `ApiCallGateway` maps the authenticated `KonnexApiClient`; the server store is the single authority; `KonnexCallSurface` maps `CallState` onto the foreground service, `CallStyle` notification and self-managed Telecom, and forwards their user actions back.

## 4. Design and implementation

- **Server:** new `calls` table (schema v12), `startCall/acceptCall/rejectCall/hangupCall` with membership checks for **both** parties inside the write transaction, one live call per account, 45 s ring deadline applied lazily and conditionally on `RINGING`, monotonic `revision`, idempotent repeats.
- **Routes:** `POST /v1/calls`, `GET /v1/calls/pending`, `GET /v1/calls/{id}`, `POST /v1/calls/{id}/{accept,reject,hangup}`; non-participants get `404` (no call-existence oracle); per-account 300 req/min limiter.
- **Client:** `CallCoordinator` rejects stale revisions, refuses a local `accept` when the device is not the callee, ends a vanished live call with `NETWORK_ERROR`, leaves a call untouched on a transport error, and moves the UI to `Ended` immediately on hangup.

## 5. Lifecycle and state management

`Idle → Dialing → Connecting → Active → Ended(reason)` with `Ringing` for incoming; accepted/declined/cancelled/missed/timeout/network-error all reach `Ended`; a terminal snapshot clears `activeCall` so accept/reject cannot target a finished call. Server timeout is authoritative; the local `isPastRingDeadline` helper exists but the server's own deadline wins.

## 6. Client implementation

New `domain:calling` coordinator (15 tests), `core:network` call DTOs and six client methods, `calling` gateway adapter, `KonnexCallManager.capabilities` now reports `signallingImplemented/telecomIntegrated/foregroundServiceImplemented = true`, `voiceImplemented/videoImplemented = false`.

## 7. Server implementation

`CallDtos.kt`, `CallRoutes.kt`, store methods and migration, `ServerModule` wiring + limiter. No media, SDP or ICE anywhere.

## 8. Files changed

## 1. Initial Git audit

Branch `main`, HEAD `4a2af8f67924702a81e16a6519d1bdce562f99e3` (`docs: correct the Stage 6.1 JVM test delta`), index **empty**, working tree with **47 pre-existing entries** (18 modified, 29 untracked) from Phase 1–5 work. All 47 were preserved. Notable exclusions: `API_SPEC.md`, `app/build.gradle.kts` (its 11 added lines are a Phase 1.2 debug ABI filter), `KeystoreDatabaseKeyProvider.kt`, `DeviceKeyMaterialStore.kt`, the entire `domain/sync` + `sync` set, and `server/api/{Dtos,Routes,Validation}.kt`.

## 2. Root causes

Stage 6.1 could ring and manage a call but never carry one: (a) no real-time transport — polling costs a round trip per ICE candidate and cannot *push* "call over"; (b) no message-level dedupe/ordering/stale rejection, so a late frame could revive a dead call; (c) no media engine and no ICE servers; (d) no audio policy, so a call would fight music/navigation and route audio wrongly; (e) no media lifecycle guaranteeing microphone/camera release; (f) **the call surface was dead code** — `startCallSurface` existed but nothing in the app called it.

## 3. Architecture

HTTPS stays authoritative for call state (revisions, 45 s ring timeout); a single authenticated WebSocket (`WS /v1/calls/{id}/ws`) carries negotiation; every frame is also written to `call_signals`, and `GET /v1/calls/{id}/signals?afterSeq=` replays what a dropped socket missed — so the socket is a transport, not a second source of truth. Only the caller offers, so glare is structurally impossible. Renegotiation is a new offer from `STABLE`, which is how video is enabled on a voice call.

## 4. Design and implementation

Typed frames (`OFFER`, `ANSWER`, `ICE_CANDIDATE`, `ICE_COMPLETE`, `TERMINATED`) with a client message id; ICE payloads carry `mline`/`mid` because libwebrtc needs the m-line index to attach a candidate. Limits: 48 KiB frame, 32 KiB SDP, 1 KiB single-line candidate, id `[A-Za-z0-9:_-]{1,128}`. Server dedupe on `UNIQUE(call_id, sender_user_id, client_message_id)`; `seq` is `AUTOINCREMENT` and **may have gaps**, so clients compare order, never `seq + 1`. Client policy: three-state phase machine, candidate buffer before SDP (bounded to 64), ICE restart after an 8 s `DISCONNECTED` grace, immediate restart on `FAILED`, bounded restart budget, exactly-once teardown. Engine is `io.github.webrtc-sdk:android:144.7559.15` behind a `MediaEngine` seam — `WebRtcMediaEngine` is the only file importing `org.webrtc`. TURN credentials are coturn `TURN REST API` (HMAC-SHA1, per call, 600 s) from `KONNEX_TURN_SHARED_SECRET`; nothing hardcoded, and an unconfigured deployment answers `relayConfigured=false` with STUN only.

## 5. Lifecycle and state management

Media attaches only in `Active` and detaches on any terminal state, including a server-pushed `TERMINATED`. `stop()` is idempotent (tracks, capturer, peer connection, ADM, EGL, audio focus, audio mode all released), so a double end cannot double-free. `phoneCall|microphone|camera` are declared statically but requested per call and only with the matching runtime permission — Android 14's `SecurityException` path is unreachable by construction. `AppContainer.ensureCallSurface()` now starts the surface once per process with a 3 s poll loop from `MainActivity.onStart()`, which is what made Stage 6.1's surface live.

## 6. Client implementation

`domain:calling` holds everything decidable without Android: `CallSignalling.kt` (validation + phase machine + dedupe + ICE buffering + close), `CallMediaEngine.kt` (`offerer` flag, `IceCandidatePayload`), `CallMediaController.kt` (restart budget, teardown). `core:network` holds `CallMediaDtos` (redacting `toString`) and `CallSignallingSocket` (bearer header on upgrade, never in a URL, `HELLO` with last `seq`). `calling` holds `WebRtcMediaEngine`, `CallAudioManager`, `CallMediaSession`, `KonnexCallVideoView`. Mute is `setEnabled(false)` rather than releasing the microphone (no renegotiation, reliable resume); a video call without camera permission is refused with a reason, not silently downgraded.

## 7. Server implementation

Schema **v13** `call_signals` (+ index), `appendCallSignal` transactional and liveness-checked, `callSignalsSince`, `lastCallSignalSeq`; `CallMediaRoutes` (WS, resync, TURN credentials); `CallSignalHub` (8 connections/call, 3/account, 128 queued frames); `CallAuth` shared by `CallRoutes` and the media routes; limits 900 signal frames/min and 300 call HTTP requests/min. The relay stores and fans out; it never parses or rewrites SDP.

## 8. Files changed

**46 files: 22 added, 24 modified**, +6,102/−294. 17 new sources, 5 new reports; 5 living docs updated.

## 9. JVM results

`./gradlew test --rerun-tasks` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**, **211 suites / 2,051 tests / 0 failures / 0 skipped** (6.1: 209 / 2,010). Delta +41: `CallSignallingSessionTest` (22) and `CallMediaControllerTest` (19); `domain:calling` now holds 63 tests.

## 10. Server results

`cd server && ../gradlew --no-build-cache test --rerun-tasks` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL** (6m21s), **34 suites / 300 tests / 0 failures** (6.1: 33 / 286). `CallMediaSignallingTest` (14) covers socket auth, non-participant refusal, HELLO, relay, terminal refusal, malformed/oversized frames, resend-relayed-once, resync and its authorization, TURN shape, unconfigured-TURN honesty, revoked-session refusal.

## 11. API 35 instrumentation

On `emulator-5554` only; the two attached phones were never touched and `connectedDebugAndroidTest` was not run. **`CallMediaInstrumentedTest` OK (8 tests)**, **`CallSurfaceTest` OK (10 tests)** — 18 tests, 0 failures. Two real findings fixed: `GrantPermissionRule` is unavailable (`androidx.test:rules` is not a dependency), so permissions are granted via `UiAutomation`; and revoking a runtime permission **kills the app process**, so denial is exercised through a `Context` reporting `PERMISSION_DENIED` — the same call the production gate makes.

## 12. Build results

Debug `210,805,073 B` (+28,296,343), release `362,485,530 B` (+47,907,231), androidTest `1,371,732 B`. Debug/androidTest assemble 4m30s, release 1m52s, **R8-enabled release (`-PkonnexMinifyRelease=true`) succeeds** with `-keep class org.webrtc.**`. Native `libjingle_peerconnection_so.so` verified for all four ABIs (12.1/6.8/12.6/16.1 MB), which is exactly the size delta.

## 13. Security assessment

Every signalling route and frame is session-authenticated, participant-checked, liveness-checked and rate-limited; sender identity and `seq` are server-derived; duplicates and replays are inert on both sides; terminal calls refuse frames at the store; a revoked session loses its socket. TURN secrets exist only server-side; credentials are per call, short-lived and redacted in logs. **DTLS-SRTP is transport encryption, not E2EE against the signalling server** — stated in `KonnexCallManager`/`KonnexCallSurface` notes, the conversation notice and `SECURITY.md`; `endToEndEncryptionImplemented` stays `false` and `E2eeSessionPolicy(enabled=false)` is untouched. No production E2EE gate was opened.

## 14. Documentation

New: `KONNEX_STAGE_6_2_MEDIA_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `..._WEBRTC_REPORT.md`, `..._SECURITY_REPORT.md`, `..._TEST_REPORT.md`, `..._FINAL_REPORT.md`. Updated: `CALL_ENGINE.md` (rewritten for the media era), `SECURITY.md` (+47/−0), `README.md` (+39/−0), backlog (6.2 checked, 6.3 outlined), six-stage status. `API_SPEC.md` was **not** updated because it is one of the 47 pre-existing modified files — mixing it in would have violated the preservation rule; the new endpoints are documented in `CALL_ENGINE.md` §5 and the architecture report.

## 16. Limitations and next milestone

**Not tested, therefore not claimed:** a call between two real installations (only one AVD; no second peer, no mock substituted — bidirectional audio/video is **unverified**); TURN relay, restrictive NAT and TURN over TLS (no relay deployed); Bluetooth routing, hardware AEC and audio/video quality; Wi-Fi ↔ mobile switching and mid-call loss; **the in-app in-call screen** (`KonnexCallVideoView` exists, no screen hosts it, so video is captured and transported but not shown); automatic socket reconnect (`HELLO`/resync make it possible, no retry loop drives it); Stage 6.1's `DeviceRevocation`/`PushRuntime` instrumentation was not re-run.

**Stage 6.3:** deploy coturn and prove a relay-only call across restrictive NAT; two-device and multi-network validation; reliability under Doze/OEM background restrictions; quality adaptation and battery/memory profiling; in-call screen; independent security review of calling and signalling. NAS/WebDAV/SFTP/private-server storage remain deferred and untouched.

## 1. Initial Git audit

Branch `main`, HEAD `cedb7d7` (Stage 6.2 docs correction), index **empty**, working tree with the same **47 pre-existing entries** (18 modified, 29 untracked) from Phase 1–5. All preserved and never staged; re-verified as 47 outside the index after committing. `API_SPEC.md`, `app/build.gradle.kts`, the `sync`/`domain:sync` set, `core/security` and three pre-existing server tests were deliberately excluded.

## 2. Root causes

1. An answered call had **no screen**: the engine and `KonnexCallVideoView` existed, nothing hosted them, so video was captured and never shown.
2. A dropped signalling socket was **permanent** — 6.2 logged it and carried on silently.
3. A Wi-Fi↔mobile switch was invisible until the 8 s `DISCONNECTED` grace noticed dead candidates.
4. Nothing **measured** quality, so the UI could not distinguish a healthy call from an unusable one.
5. TURN had credentials but no deployment story, no URL validation, no TTL bound, no way to verify a relay.

## 3. Architecture

The server stays authoritative; `WS /v1/calls/{id}/ws` still fronts the durable `call_signals` log. New layering: `:core:network` is a **single-connection** transport exposing `connectionLost` (no retry policy, no domain dependency); retry policy lives in `:domain:calling` (`ReconnectPolicy` + `SignallingReconnector`); `:calling` wires them with resync and owns the network monitor and quality cadence; `:app` hosts the screen; `deploy/coturn` holds the relay.

## 4. Design and implementation

- **Reconnection**: 6 attempts, 500 ms base, 30 s cap, ±20% jitter; token re-read per attempt; on success the `HELLO` sequence drives `signals?afterSeq=`; termination checked before each attempt *and after each wait*; `close()` is terminal.
- **Network change**: default-network callback, transport-change detection, 1.5 s debounce, immediate `restartIce()` with a separate budget of 3, then the call ends rather than looping.
- **Quality**: RTT/loss/jitter/available-bitrate/relay from `getStats`; `UNKNOWN` when nothing is measured; video sender capped at 1200/600/300 kbps (30/24/15 fps).
- **UI**: one screen for every phase, pure model, `AndroidView` keyed by call id, encryption note on every active call, permissions requested before actions.
- **Relay**: coturn config (UDP/TCP/TLS, REST secret, denied private ranges, quotas, `no-cli`), compose file, deployment guide, `verify-turn.sh`; `turn:`/`turns:`-only validation; TTL clamped to 60–3600 s in config and route.

## 5. Lifecycle and state management

The call lives in `AppContainer`; the screen is a projection. Rotation recreates composition, not the call; `AndroidView.onRelease` frees renderers. Media still attaches only in `Active` and detaches on every terminal path with idempotent teardown. `detach()` now also stops the link job, quality job and network monitor and resets link state/quality. A lost link sets `LOST` without ending the call — media policy decides. Notification permission is requested on first appearance so a ring is not silent.

## 6. Client implementation

`domain:calling`: `SignallingRecovery.kt`, `MediaQuality.kt`, `CallUiModel.kt`, plus `CallMediaController` (network restarts, quality) and `CallMediaEngine` (`stats()`, `applyVideoQuality()`, defaulted so fakes stay valid). `core:network`: `CallSignallingSocket` rewritten as single-connection. `calling`: `CallNetworkMonitor`, `CallMediaSession` (link loop, resync, quality polling, monitor), `KonnexCallSurface` accessors/actions, `WebRtcMediaEngine` statistics parsing and sender caps. `app`: `call/KonnexCallScreen.kt`, `AppContainer.callSurfaceFlow`, `KonnexRoot` mounts the host above the graph.

## 7. Server implementation

`TurnEndpoints` accepts only `turn:`/`turns:`; TTL clamped in `ServerConfig.fromEnv` **and** at mint time; the TURN response is built only from filtered URLs. Signalling, dedupe, resync and terminal refusal are unchanged and re-tested.

Modified: 2 domain, 3 `calling`, 1 `core:network`, 2 app, 2 server, 5 living docs.

## 13. Security assessment

Reconnection is bounded, jittered, cancelled on termination and refused by the server for terminal calls, so it cannot hammer the server or resurrect a call. Network-driven ICE restarts are debounced and capped. TURN credentials are per call and participant, TTL-clamped, HMAC-verifiable by coturn, never in a response or log; the relay denies loopback/link-local/private peers and the CLI; only `turn:`/`turns:` URLs reach clients. The screen states that DTLS-SRTP is transport encryption, **not** E2EE against the signalling server; `endToEndEncryptionImplemented` stays `false` and the E2EE policy remains disabled. Residual: no independent review, no relay deployed, no real restart or network switch.

Stage 6.4 is implemented, tested on the API 35 emulator, documented and committed locally. Two commits, nothing pushed, and the working tree is back to exactly the 47 pre-existing entries.

## 1. Initial Git audit

Branch `main`, HEAD `84f411f` (Stage 6.3), index empty, **47 pre-existing entries** (18 modified, 29 untracked) — all preserved, none staged. Baseline recorded before editing: JVM 214 suites / 2,088 tests, server 35 / 310, instrumentation 26, debug APK 211,170,548 B.

## 2. Root causes addressed

1. **No measured evidence about a call** — 6.3 produced an estimate but never establishment latency, reconnect counts or whether TURN carried the media, so a real run had nothing to record and the UI could not say which path was in use.
2. **Adaptive quality oscillated** — one sample changed the sender cap; on a real network that means switching profiles for the whole call.
3. **Reconnection reused a possibly expired token** — a call outliving its access token could loop on `Unauthorized` until the attempt budget died.
4. **No operational view of the relay** — verifiable only by placing a call, and `verify-turn.sh` printed prose instead of verdicts.
5. **Production safety net untested** — socket caps, refreshed-token rejoin and restart durability had no tests.

## 3. Architecture

Unchanged layering: `:domain:calling` pure, `:calling` wires media/signalling, `:app` composes, server owns call state and the durable signal log. Added: `CallSessionMetrics` and `VideoQualityGovernor` in the domain, metrics/governor wiring plus session refresh in `CallMediaController`/`CallMediaSession`, `GET /v1/health/calling`, `deploy/coturn/healthcheck.sh`, rewritten `verify-turn.sh`.

## 4. TURN production deployment

Reviewed and hardened the existing config (UDP/TCP 3478, TLS 5349, `no-cli`, denied loopback/private/link-local peer ranges, explicit relay range, REST credentials). New `GET /v1/health/calling` reports `relayConfigured`, usable `turn:`/`turns:` counts and the TTL, with a test asserting it contains neither the shared secret nor the relay hostname. TTL stays clamped 60–3600 s at config load and mint. `verify-turn.sh` now prints **PASS/FAIL/SKIP** per check, exits non-zero on failure, and has a credential-free `--health` mode that probes 3478/tcp and 5349/tcp. `healthcheck.sh` checks process, listeners, config permissions, leftover placeholders, secret length (never printed), certificate validity and relay range. **No relay was deployed — no coturn, no Docker, no public IP — so no allocation is claimed.**

## 5. Two-device calling validation

**Not performed.** Only `emulator-5554` exists, no second installation was possible, and the attached phones (`LGG710PMa2a99b5a`, `R9WW20J39TF`) were never targeted. `KONNEX_STAGE_6_4_TWO_DEVICE_TEST_REPORT.md` records the environment inventory, what was substituted (26 instrumentation, 15 server and 119 domain tests), the empty matrix a real run must fill, and the exact procedure including `verify-turn.sh`.

## 6. Network reliability

Bounded by construction and tested: 6 reconnect attempts (500 ms → 30 s, ±20% jitter), 3 network restarts, 3 ICE restarts, one forced token refresh per attempt; per-frame session re-check; terminal calls refuse reconnection; frames survive a process restart and resync by `afterSeq`; per-account (3) and per-call (8) socket caps. New server evidence: `one account cannot open unbounded signalling sockets`, `a refreshed token can rejoin the signalling socket`, `signalling frames survive a server restart`. Real hardware switching, Doze, live-socket restart and mid-call TURN expiry remain untested and are listed as such.

## 7. Android production validation

API 35 emulator: debug and androidTest APKs installed (`Success`), all three classes run, `logcat -b crash` empty afterwards. Lock screen, rotation with live video, background/foreground with a real peer, process-death recovery and physical-device logs are **not verified** — stated in `KONNEX_STAGE_6_4_PRODUCTION_VALIDATION.md`.

## 1. Initial Git audit

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch / HEAD | `main` / `12787c2` (Stage 6.4 docs fix) |

## 2. Root causes

A real two-endpoint call was run for the first time; it exposed defects that single-engine tests structurally could not see.

| # | Defect | Effect | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Candidate pair never resolved | relay usage and RTT permanently `null` on device | parser compared `state == "SUCCEEDED"`; libwebrtc reports `succeeded` |
| 2 | `CONNECTED` rolled back to `CONNECTING` | screen stuck on “Connecting…”, establishment never measured | `applyRemoteDescription` wrote `CONNECTING` unconditionally |
| 3 | `addSink(null)` throws | video capture/receive failed without a bound renderer | every sink binding assumed a non-null view |
| 4 | Front camera required | rear-camera-only devices could not send video | camera picked by facing, no fallback |
| 5 | Full-screen intent targeted a service | a locked phone never showed an incoming call | Android launches an *activity* for full-screen intents |
| 6 | Ended call had no exit | dead call screen covered the app after every call | `Ended` is terminal and nothing left it |
| 7 | Answer after process death dropped | user taps Answer, nothing happens | dispatch could not report “no surface” |

## 3. Architecture

`domain:calling` stayed pure Kotlin (new `Dismissed` event, `canDismiss`, `videoSummary`, decoded-frame fields, per-outage restart budget). `calling` gained `KonnexCallIntents` as the ringing-call intent contract and fixed the engine’s stats/camera/sink handling. `app` only wires it: `MainActivity` applies keyguard/wake flags **only** for a call launch; the call host renders Done and auto-dismisses. No server production code changed.

## 4. Two-device validation

**Not performed** — one AVD, no second installation target, physical phones excluded by standing instruction. Substituted with a real two-endpoint call in one process (`CallLoopbackInstrumentedTest`): real ICE, DTLS-SRTP, RTP, `getStats`.

Measured once on `emulator-5554`: establishment **727 ms**, **direct host** candidate pair, RTT **1 ms**, jitter **0 ms**, loss **0.0 %**, 300 kbps initial estimate, audio both ways, video upgrade decoding **320×240**, both engines released. Android-to-Android over a network remains unverified.

## 5. TURN production verification

**No allocation was performed**: no coturn, no Docker, no public IP, no TLS certificate. Verified instead: REST credential algorithm, TTL clamping, per-participant scoping, URL filtering, secret absence, honest STUN-only answer, and that a direct path is measured as direct. UDP/TCP/TLS allocation, expiry/rotation mid-call and relay-only connectivity are unverified; the runbook and scripts are ready for an operator.

## 6. Network reliability

- Network restarts are now budgeted **per outage** and replenished by a reconnect: three switches each followed by `CONNECTED` no longer end a call; three without a reconnect still do (JVM tests both ways).
- State can no longer be rolled back from `CONNECTED`.
- New server guarantee: a revoked session cannot open a socket, resync or mint TURN credentials.
- Real Wi-Fi↔mobile switching, congestion, Doze and credential expiry mid-call: **not tested**.

## 7. Android lifecycle

Fixed lock-screen incoming call (activity-backed full-screen intent + keyguard/wake flags only for that launch), ended-call dismissal, Answer after process death, video without a renderer, rear-camera-only devices. Verified on API 35 by instrumentation. Locked-device wake-up, rotation with live video, background audio, Bluetooth and Doze remain **untested** (need hardware).

## 8. Files changed

33 files, +1,841/−54. New: `KonnexCallIntents.kt`, `CallLoopbackInstrumentedTest.kt`, eight `KONNEX_STAGE_6_5_*.md`. Modified: five `domain/calling` sources, four `calling` sources, `MainActivity`, `KonnexCallScreen`, five test files, `CallReliabilityTest`, and `CALL_ENGINE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `README.md`, backlog, six-stage status.

## 9. JVM results

One `--rerun-tasks` execution reported a single failure in **unrelated** `data:messaging` (`MultiDeviceFanOutTest`, “could not generate a larger peer identity”); that class passes 3/3 in isolation, so it is recorded as flaky — not fixed, not weakened.

## 10. Server results

`--no-build-cache --rerun-tasks` — **35 suites, 316 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped** (+1 revocation test). The new test initially asserted a failed WebSocket handshake; the server actually closes with policy violation 1008, so the assertion was corrected to match the real contract rather than the test being relaxed.

## 13. Security assessment

No new defect; one control strengthened (revoked sessions cannot re-enter) and one behaviour improved (Answer no longer dropped). Notifications still carry only a name and call id; only the call launch may pass the keyguard. `E2eeSessionPolicy(enabled = false)` and `endToEndEncryptionImplemented = false` unchanged — **calls remain DTLS-SRTP, not E2EE**.

The six-stage roadmap keeps Stage 5 storage items and call E2EE deferred, not completed.
